name: Cowpea Mosaic Virus
description: A viral disease causing mosaic patterns, leaf distortion, and stunted growth in cowpea. It is transmitted by beetles and can cause significant yield losses in susceptible varieties across West Africa.
symptoms: Yellow and green mosaic pattern on leaves
Stunted plant growth with shortened internodes
Reduced pod set and deformed seeds
Plants may show general chlorosis and reduced vigor
causes: Cowpea mosaic virus (CPMV) transmitted by leaf-feeding beetles
High beetle populations during rainy season
Infected crop debris from previous season
Alternative weed hosts serving as virus reservoirs
seasonality: Early to mid rainy season (beetle peak)
treatments: No curative treatment for viral infection
Rogue and destroy infected plants early
Control beetle vectors with appropriate insecticides
Apply neem-based sprays to deter beetles
prevention: Plant virus-tolerant cowpea varieties (e.g., IT series)
Practice early planting to avoid peak beetle populations
Use adequate plant spacing to reduce disease spread
Remove weed hosts near cowpea fields
